title: A day in the forest
body: Benda lives in a tiny village of three huts deep in the forests of the Abujh Maad area of central India. His tribe practises shifting cultivation: small patches of forest are burnt to clear them, and the ash is used to make the soil fertile. Benda feels lucky to be part of the forest of Mahua, Palash and Sal trees that has sheltered him since childhood. When he drinks from a stream he thanks Loi-Lugi, the spirit of the forest. He eats leaves and roots, and searches for special herbs that his people barter at the tribal fair (madhai), relying on what the elders taught him about where the herbs grow. When outsiders arrive, Benda and his friends vanish into the thick canopy of trees.
